validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/SOURCING CONCERN. No independent source confirms this specific pipeline. The name decodes to a route-segment descriptor, not a reportable named pipeline: 'UBTG' = Uthmaniyah-Berri-Tanajib-Ghawar gas network (part of Saudi Aramco's Master Gas System; this much IS independently attested via MEED/Aramco/pipeline-journal coverage of the UBTG and MGS systems), 'km56' = kilometer 56 on the UBTG-1 line, and 'AY-1 KP916' = kilometer-post 916 on the Abqaiq-Yanbu Oil Line I (AY-1) crude line (offshore-technology.com confirms Abqaiq-Yanbu Oil Line I: 1,204 km, up to 56-inch, Eastern Province->Al Madinah, crude oil, operating since 1987). So the GEM row describes a gas segment running from km56 of the UBTG line to KP916 (a point alongside the crude AY-1 corridor). Web searches in English (and the broad MGS/UBTG literature) return the segment name 'UBTG-km56-AY-1 KP916' ONLY on gem.wiki itself and GEM-derived echoes; no media, Aramco, SPA, Argaam, or trade source independently reports this segment, its 244 km length, its 56-inch diameter, or its endpoints. The two refs attached to the gem.wiki page are generic OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletins (ASB2012 PDF, ASB2013 p.79) that report only aggregate Saudi pipeline statistics, not this individual line. I verified the ASB2012 PDF returns HTTP 200 but it does NOT contain segment-specific 'pipeline' content matching this row (url_verifier FAIL on token 'pipeline'); the ASB2013 flipbook page returns HTTP 403. Net: the underlying UBTG/MGS network and the Aramco ownership are real and the gas-commodity classification is plausible, but THIS specific kilometer-post-named segment is a GEM-only entity with no independent corroboration of existence or specs — consistent with extraction from a route/GIS dataset that sliced a trunk line into KP-labeled segments (cf. sibling rows P1910/P1911/P1912 'UBTG-1-km0-UBTG-1-km56' and P1903 'AY-1 KP 943-Riyadh', which share the same artificial KP-naming pattern and may be co-slices of the same physical infrastructure). Possible duplicate/segment-double-count risk with the UBTG-1 cluster, but I could not confirm a specific overlapping PID from independent sources, so logging the primary concern as existence.

summary: P1900 UBTG-km56-AY-1 KP916: existence/sourcing concern — GEM-only kilometer-post-named gas segment; UBTG/MGS network + Aramco ownership are real, but no independent source confirms this specific segment, its 244 km length, 56-inch diameter, or endpoints (cited OPEC ASBs are generic and one is dead/403). No verifiable independent ref obtained; all value cells UNRESOLVED.
